title: Lüroth's theorem for a nonconstant rational intermediate field
statement: Let $F$ be a field [def-weil-field] and let $F(T)$ be its one-variable rational function field [def-weil-rational-function-field]. Let $E$ be an intermediate field: a subset of $F(T)$ containing the image of $F$ and closed under addition, subtraction, multiplication and inversion of nonzero elements, with the induced field and $F$-algebra structure [def-pc-field-extension]. If $E$ is strictly larger than the constant subfield $F$, then there is an $F$-algebra isomorphism $F(T)\simeq E$. No perfectness, algebraic closedness or characteristic hypothesis is required.
